notes: Company background: mid-market billing SaaS for subscription businesses (Stripe + Zuora connectors). 450 employees, US HQ.

Primary ask: replace brittle rule-based chat assistant for support team with an LLM-powered agent that can stream responses and call external tools (Stripe / Zuora) to issue refunds, look up invoices, and surface structured JSON outputs for downstream automation.

Latency SLOs: first-token streaming target ~<200ms for typical short queries; end-to-end action (tool-call + ack) under 800ms in 95th percentile during off-peak; peak throughput target ~150-250 reqs/sec for busy billing hours.

POC scope agreed: 2-week hosted API POC using production-like traffic (sanitized logs), validate streaming latency, tool-calling reliability, and structured JSON schema output for 'refund' and 'billing_summary' actions.
Security: PCI-in-scope for payment actions (only tokenized IDs passed), must satisfy SOC2 controls and SSO (SAML) audit. Evaluate VPC/Dedicated for scope reduction if hosted cannot meet PCI guidance.
Cost sensitivity: currently modelled at break-even around 1.8-2.2M tokens/month; finance wants a dedicated reserved option if sustained usage exceeds that range.

Model preferences: prefer open models with deterministic structured output and good tool-call semantics; will accept Redwood-verified model profiles. Want ability to pin model versions and automatic fallback to cheaper variants when latency allows.

Integration notes: Stripe refund flow must be atomic from agent perspective — LLM issues JSON payload with 'charge_id' + 'reason', Redwood function-call should hit internal service for idempotency and then call Stripe. Need audit logs for every tool-call.

Quote from Head of Product: 'We need streaming that actually feels live for agents — sub-200ms first token is non-negotiable. And if the agent calls Stripe, we need immediate structured confirmation back.'
Quote from Security: 'If hosted path cannot remove PCI data from Redwood's scope we will require Dedicated or Private deployment.'

Evaluation criteria: latency (first token & tail), tool-call durability (retries, idempotency), structured-output reliability (JSON schema validation rate), cost per ticket, and auditability (per-request logs + KMS integration).
Decision drivers: performance demo (this week), security sign-off on SAML docs (next week), finance sign-off on ARR model (mid-April).

Next steps recorded: SE to run 48-hr perf run (Priya), product team to provide sanitized example logs and schema mapping, Redwood to provide hosted POC pricing and Dedicated reserve estimate for 12 months.
Potential blockers: PCI scoping, ambiguity on which Zuora workflows require direct system writes vs read-only lookups, data residency for certain enterprise customers.
